title: Stock Market Today Highlights, Aug 4: Markets end in the red; Sensex drops 210 points, Nifty slips 159 - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Stock Market Chart | Photo Credit: istock.com

Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Highlights: Find here all the updates related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 4th August 2026.

Indian equity benchmarks ended lower on Tuesday as investors turned cautious ahead of the Reserve Bank of India’s monetary policy decision and adjusted positions following the introduction of the new closing-auction mechanism for stocks with futures and options contracts.

The Nifty 50 declined 0.64% to 24,614.90, while the Sensex slipped 0.27% to 78,428.95, partially reversing Monday’s rally. Market volatility increased, with the India VIX rising to a one-week high ahead of the weekly Nifty derivatives expiry.

Analysts said the new auction framework triggered short-term adjustments, though its impact is expected to diminish as market participants adapt.

Higher Brent crude prices added to investor caution, raising concerns over inflation, growth and corporate earnings. Most sectoral indices ended in the red, led by financials and IT.

Among stocks, LIC plunged after the government’s stake sale announcement, while Reliance Industries, HDFC Bank and Dabur also weighed on the benchmarks.

Follow our live coverage of Q1 Results here

* Benchmark indices end lower: Sensex fell 210.08 points to 78,428.95, while Nifty declined 159.40 points to 24,614.90.

* RBI policy in focus: Investors remained cautious ahead of the Reserve Bank of India’s monetary policy decision on Wednesday.

* Volatility spikes: India VIX climbed to a one-week high ahead of the weekly Nifty derivatives expiry.

* New F&O auction impact: Market participants adjusted positions following the introduction of the closing-auction mechanism for F&O stocks, adding to intraday volatility.

* Oil prices rebound: Brent crude rose nearly 3% to around $86.2 a barrel, reviving inflation concerns.

* Broad-based selling: 15 of the 16 major sectoral indices ended lower, led by financials and IT.

* LIC tumbles: Shares of LIC slumped 8.7% after the government launched a stake sale at a discount.

* Heavyweights drag: Reliance Industries fell 2.1%, while HDFC Bank declined 1.5%, weighing on benchmark indices.

* Dabur under pressure: The FMCG stock dropped 3.8% after regulatory action over unverified product claims.

* Broader markets mixed: Small-cap stocks gained 0.2%, while the mid-cap index slipped 0.3%.

The National Stock Exchange, in an V-hour clarification, said that Closing Auction Session was implemented under the guidance of SEBI as it promotes transparency and fair and robust price discovery.

The clarification comes in the wake of ​Nifty 50’s official closing value as it jumped nearly 200 points​ on Monday after continuous trading had ended, surprising market participants on the first day of the Closing Auction Session (CAS) for stocks in the futures and options (F&O) segment. “BTC approached $64K after the ISM Manufacturing PMI rose to 55.6, its highest level since 2022. ISM is a leading indicator because purchasing managers often see shifts in demand before they appear in GDP or corporate earnings. A reading above 50 signals economic expansion, while stronger levels typically point to improving business activity and healthier risk appetite. Historically, sustained ISM readings above 55 have coincided with strong altcoin performance. If broader liquidity conditions improve alongside this trend, an altcoin season could begin to develop. Near term, $64K is resistance, while $63K remains key support,” said CoinSwitch Markets Desk.
